chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man marries a woman for her beauty or her wealth, he is entrusted to that [quality], and if he marries her for her religion, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will grant him both beauty and wealth."

key_terms.وُكِلَ إِلَى ذَلِكَ: entrusted to that / left to that consequence

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for marrying a woman for her religion according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the chain of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, emphasizing that intention (*niyyah*) dictates the divine reward structure in marriage. While marrying for worldly attributes limits one to those transient qualities, prioritizing piety (*din*) invites God to bestow both spiritual and material blessings, reflecting the Shia principle that outward beauty is a consequence of inner righteousness.
